board.title: Scanner · D · Getting in and capture: Page first, guide frame (round 2)
board.name: Page first, guide frame
board.idea: The /scanner page comes first with the step strip, the count and the whose-game chips, and one gold Take a photo button opens an in-page camera with the gold guide frame that shoots on its own when the sheet is steady.
board.differs: Scan-D opens the camera from the page and draws the camera itself (getUserMedia, gold guide frame, auto-shoot, corner marks skip the crop); Scan-E opens the phone's own camera first and checks the photo afterwards with four draggable corners.

drawn.title: Scanner · D · Getting in and capture: Page first, guide frame (round 2)
drawn.note:
What: Part 1 of the scanner (getting in and capture), option D, "Page first, guide frame". A row of six ways in leads to /scanner. Four phones show: signed out, the signed-in page (step strip, "17 of 20 scans left today", privacy line, one gold Take a photo), the in-page camera with the gold guide frame plus an inset for a printed LCA sheet, and pages chosen with the sheet's QR details. Below them sit a 1180px laptop drop zone and ten states. The other option for this part is Scan-E.

Built from: Scan-A (step strip, count, Directors button), Scan-B screen 1 (Capture) as drawn, Scan-C (TD-table card and sheet QR as ways in), and today's ScannerPage.tsx (SignInPrompt, HowItWorks, PhotoPicker, PhotoButtons, PageStrip). It uses the decided header, footer, phone app bar and tab bar. Replaces Scan-B screen 1. The "3 of 5" sample count is redrawn as the real 20 a day.

K's feedback applied: Scan-A, B and C are treated as parts of one scanner and nothing from them is dropped. This part is drawn end to end, with D and E to pick from. Open for K: photo retention ("never stored" today, or kept 30 days unless saved as drawn); who may scan and when the 20 a day resets (midnight UTC or Central); whose 20 a guardian's scan for a child counts against; and the pick between D and E.
unresolved: Scan-A's My games row 'vs Sam Nguyen · drew · Houma Chess Club night · Mon, Sep 28' falls after the drawn moment (Sun, Sep 6, 3:38 PM), so it is drawn as 'Mon, Aug 31' (still Sample data).

The spec's laptop header lists 'Donate · My LCA · Marcus Landry'. The board uses the decided signed-in header ('Donate · My LCA' with a chevron, no name), to match Tourn-List-Final and Nav-Header-Final.

The spec puts the printed-LCA-sheet inset at the bottom right of phone 3, but there it would cover the Back side button and the guide frame. It hangs off the phone's top right instead, over the empty right side of the app bar.

To keep the board under 2600px, the ten state cards sit in two columns beside the laptop (640px wide) instead of five across under it. Rendered content is 2511px; declared height and $preview are 2550.
Phone 1 (signed out) is taller than the screen: How it works steps 3 and 4 and the Print the notation kit link sit under a scroll fade marked 'Scroll for steps 3 and 4 and Print the notation kit'.

The privacy line, the How it works rail and the rules use WS15's 30-day wording ('Photos are kept 30 days unless you save the game'). Today's page, API and migration say 'never stored'; this is named as open for K in note 3 and the grey note.

review.counts:
Final size is 1960 x 2550. The content renders at 2549px, which rounds up to 2550, under the 2600 limit. The root height and $preview are both 2550. There is one file and no second part.

The board has these regions:
- **Title strip:** kicker, ROUND 2 badge, Built from, Replaces, K's feedback applied, Shown (Sun, Sep 6, 2026 at 3:38 PM) and the Sample data badge.
- **Grey note:** What / Built from / K's feedback applied / Open for K, with 4 open items.
- **Legend:** 6 numbered notes. On the design there are 10 badges: 1 x2, 2 x1, 3 x2, 4 x1, 5 x1, 6 x3.
- **A, Ways in:** 6 cards (the QR card highlighted, WS07 tagged Proposed) and a connector line into phones 1 and 2.
- **B, Phones:** 4 phones at 414px: Signed out, Signed in page, Camera with guide frame plus the printed-sheet inset, and Pages chosen.
- **C, Laptop:** 1180px, with the decided desktop header and footer (matched to Tourn-List-Final), a drop zone and no camera.
- **D, States:** 10 cards, each with a coloured dot and the state in words: Loading, Empty, Page limit, Blurry or dark, Camera refused or absent, Not a photo, Daily limit reached, Offline, A guardian's page, A director's page.

Rule checks:
- **Copy:** 0 em or en dashes, 0 USCF, 0 copy ".5" (only SVG path numbers), 0 AI references, 0 grade or birthdate.
- **Gold:** #c8a94a appears 5 times, only on the dark camera ground, the shutter ring, the step pill dot and the section-code chip. Gold-ink text uses #866a1e.
- **Dates:** every date has a weekday (Sun, Sep 6; Sat, Sep 5; Mon, Aug 31, the same as Scan-G and Scan-L). Times read 3:38 PM to 3:40 PM and 8:00 PM.
- **Count:** in words, "17 of 20 scans left today · resets at midnight", and "0 of 20" in the limit state.
- **Same game as the other parts:** Marcus Landry 2014 vs Priya Shah 1803, Board 6, Round 4, Open, Louisiana State Championship 2026, Sun, Sep 6, under the same step strip (Photo · Read · Check · Save & share).
- **Decoder contract:** "We read the handwriting · Exactly as written, mistakes included" and "Chess rules check every move". Nothing says the reader corrected a move. Save and Export are not on this part.
- **Privacy:** the guardian state shows "Priya" by first name only and "private until you allow sharing". There is no child email or grade.
- **Markup:** tags balance, the skeleton matches the template, and nothing is animated, no iframes, no {{holes}}.
- **Overflow:** after the fixes the measurement script finds no overflowing or clipped element.
changes: Phone 1 (signed out): the content was 122px taller than the screen, so How it works steps 3 and 4 and 'Print the notation kit' were hidden behind a 'Scroll for...' fade. Fixed by putting 'Log in to scan' and 'Create an account' side by side and tightening the spacing and type on that phone. All four steps and the link now show, and the fade is removed.

Phone 3 inset (printed LCA sheet): it covered the phone's status bar and top-right corner. It is now a compact 196 x 160 card in the caption band above phone 3, clear of the ways-in connector and the phone. The pill 'LCA sheet found · straightening on the corner marks' is kept. The text is shortened to 'Event, round, board and names fill in from the sheet's QR.'
To make room for the inset, phone captions grew from 66px to 104px, and phone 3's caption narrowed to 258px. The board still renders at 2549px and stays declared at 2550.
Step pills: the row was 2px wider than the phone screen, so 'Save & share' was clipped. Pill padding dropped from 12px to 11px and all four pills now fit.

Grey 'What' note: added 'Scan-E instead opens the phone's own camera first and checks the photo with four draggable corners.' This makes the difference from Scan-E clear at a glance. I tried it in the title strip first, but it pushed the board past 2550.
remaining_concerns: The spec asks for the printed-sheet inset 'at the bottom right of the phone'. There was no clear spot there: it would hide the Back side button or run into the States panel. It now sits above phone 3's top right instead, which is a small departure from the spec.
The guardian's 'Whose game is this? You · Priya' chips appear only as state card 9, not on a phone, as the spec lays out. A guardian looking at the phones alone will not see them.

The legend says Scan-A's Directors button heads the page 'at every width'. On the phone it appears only in state card 10, and on the laptop it is in the right rail with a 'directors only' tag (both as the spec says), not up with the step strip.

Photo retention is drawn as WS15's 30-day version throughout (sign-in rules, privacy lines, laptop rail). This is flagged in the grey note and in legend note 3 as open for K. If K picks 'never stored', every one of those lines needs redrawing.
My games shows 'Mon, Aug 31' rather than the spec's 'Mon, Sep 28', because Sep 28 comes after the drawn moment (Sun, Sep 6). Scan-G and Scan-L use the same Aug 31 date, so I left it.

board.title: Scanner · E · Getting in and capture: Camera first, check the photo (round 2)
board.name: Camera first, check the photo
board.idea: On a phone the scanner opens straight into the phone's own camera, and the photo is checked afterwards with four draggable corners and 'Is the whole grid in the frame?', with whose game asked at Save from the names read off the sheet.
board.differs: Scan-E keeps no camera code (today's capture=environment input) and adds a photo check with four draggable corners that works on any sheet, in poor light and at every width; Scan-D draws its own camera with a guide frame and auto-shoot and asks whose game before shooting.

drawn.title: Scanner · E · Getting in and capture: Camera first, check the photo (round 2)
drawn.note:
What: Part 1 of the scanner (getting in and capture), option 2 of 2, camera first. On a phone, Scoresheet scanner opens straight into the phone's own camera. Back on the page, the photo is checked with four draggable gold corners and the question "Is the whole grid in the frame?". The phone shows the page strip with today's "Does the game continue" copy, and whose game is asked at Save, where the names read off the sheet suggest the profile ("This looks like Priya's game"). The board also has the six ways in, a 1180px laptop with the same check (the drop zone shown as an inset) and the ten states. The drawn moment is Sun, Sep 6, 3:38 PM, Board 6, Round 4.

Built from: Scan-A's step strip, the count (redrawn as the real limit, "17 of 20 scans left today") and the Directors button. Today's ScannerPage.tsx: the capture=environment input, PhotoButtons, PageStrip, SignInPrompt and HowItWorks copy. Scan-C's sheet QR as a way in (state 9). The decided header, footer, app bar and tab bar. It replaces Scan-B screen 1. Scan-D is option 1 for this part.

K's feedback applied, and what is open for K: the board treats the scanner as one tool in parts, with two options per part, and nothing from Scan-A, B or C is turned down. The six numbered notes show where each part landed. Open for K: how long the photo is kept (the board draws WS15's 30 days unless the game is saved; today's page says photos are never stored); who may scan, and whether the 20-a-day limit resets at midnight Central; whether a guardian's scan is filed under the child and stays private until sharing is allowed; and which option to pick for part 1, this board or Scan-D.
unresolved: States are drawn two across, in five rows beside the laptop, instead of five across. Five across would have pushed the board past the 2600px limit; the states section label says where they are.
Scan-D was not in the project folder when I drew this, so Row 1 (Ways in) copies the six cards from Scan-D's spec text, not from its file. Check that the two rows match once Scan-D exists.
The spec puts the count 'in the app bar'. To keep the decided app bar unchanged, phone 1 shows it on a navy sub-bar under the app bar: 'Scoresheet scanner · 17 of 20 scans left today'.
On phone 2 the count shares the step-strip row, as the spec asks, but at 390px it has to wrap to two lines ('17 of 20 scans / left today').

The spec asks for the laptop drop zone and the four-corner check in the same main column. The drop zone is shown as a tagged inset ('Before a photo is chosen · shared with Scan-D') inside the check card's side column, not as a separate full-width zone.
The board is 2550px tall when rendered, so the declared height and $preview are both 2550, under the 2600px limit. No second board was needed.

review.counts:
Scan-E is a single file with no second part, so second_height is 0. The board renders at 2546px, so the declared height and $preview are 2550, under the 2600 limit. Nothing clips at 1960px. The only overflow is in thumbnails that crop on purpose: the page 1 thumbnail and the blurry-photo mini.

The same game, names, event, step strip (Photo · Read · Check · Save & share) and daily count ("17 of 20 scans left today", "0 of 20 scans left today") appear as in the other parts.
changes: Phone 4, the rest of the Save card: the whole section was at 55% opacity, which left the key privacy line 'Sharing a junior's game needs a guardian's OK' and the 'Who can see it' choices too faint to read. The section is now a dashed, grey-ground card. Only the photo checkbox and the Save button are dimmed, because they belong to part 5.

Phone 4: the guardian line is now full-contrast navy with a lock icon and reads 'Sharing a junior's game needs a guardian's OK. Link and Public are off until then.' The disabled 'Anyone with the link' and 'Public' buttons get a hatched ground and readable grey text, so their off state no longer depends on fading.

Title strip: added a 'Differs from Scan-D' line so the difference shows at a glance: no camera of our own, the phone's camera opens at once, four draggable corners check the photo afterwards, and whose game is asked at Save, against Scan-D's own camera with a guide frame and auto-shoot that asks whose game before shooting.
Title strip: shortened 'Built from' to one line, and the root's bottom padding went from 24px to 20px, so the new line fits and the render stays at 2546px. Declared height and $preview stay at 2550.
remaining_concerns: The spec asks for the ten state cards five across in a row of their own. The designer put them two across beside the laptop. A separate row would add about 450px and push the board past the 2600px limit, so I left the layout as drawn. The cards and their copy match the spec.

The count copy follows the parts spec: 'resets at midnight'. Today's code resets at midnight UTC, which is 7:00 PM in Louisiana in summer, and moving it to midnight Central is still an open question for K. The board lists it under Open for K but does not name the UTC time.

The guardian in phone 4, Nisha Shah, and the 15-year-old in state 10 are invented sample people. Both carry Sample tags and the title strip has the Sample data badge. Confirm the guardian's name matches whatever the other parts use (for example Scan-H and Scan-I on Save).

The laptop row is set at 8:00 PM, with Marcus at home choosing a photo. That matches Scan-D's laptop, but the flow has Marcus scanning at the venue at 3:40 PM and only opening the draft at 8:00 PM, so the laptop is really a second scenario rather than the drawn moment.
The canvas sticky can reuse the grey note's What line: 'Camera first: the phone's own camera opens at once, four corners check the photo, Save asks whose game.'

board.title: Scanner · F · The reading job and its progress: Moves stream in (round 2)
board.name: Moves stream in
board.idea: The moves appear on the phone as they are read, with the unclear cell flagged the instant it is reached, and the page hands straight over to the review when the job is done.
board.differs: Scan-F streams the moves and the four stage rows live on the screen (Scan-B screen 2 as drawn) and opens the review itself when done; Scan-G shows one quiet card, streams nothing, and hands the job off to My games, an email and a to-do so the player can scan the next sheet at once.

drawn.title: Scanner · F · The reading job and its progress: Moves stream in (round 2)
drawn.note:
What: Part 2 of the scanner, option F. Reading is a job. The moves appear on the phone as they are read, the unclear cell is flagged the moment the reading line reaches it, and the review opens by itself when the job ends. The board has the job drawn as a six-stop track, four phones (Sending, Reading, Checking every move is legal, Ready), the My games rows while the job runs, and twelve states, each with its colour and the state in words.

Built from: Scan-B screen 2 (Reading) as drawn, today's working, unreadable and error stages and their copy (ScannerPage.tsx, functions/api/scan), and WS15's async job (POST /api/scan/jobs, GET /api/scan/jobs/:id) with My games. It replaces Scan-B screen 2. The "3 of 5" sample count is redrawn as the real 20 (16 of 20 after the scan is held), the old app bar now uses the decided chrome, and today's single in-request scan becomes the async job.

K's feedback applied: Scan-A, B and C are parts of one scanner, not rivals, and nothing from them is turned down. This part is drawn in full, with F and G to pick from. Open for K: photo retention (drawn as kept for the job and then 30 days unless saved; today says never stored); the count (a scan is held when the job starts and handed back if the read fails; reset at midnight UTC or midnight Central); a guardian's scan for Priya (whose 20 it counts against, first name only, family only); pick F or G.

Its sheet has no '#, White, Black' header row (phone 2 keeps it), and its progress bar sits inside the 'Checking every move is legal' row, as on Scan-B, instead of on its own line. review.counts:

board.title: Scanner · H · Review: photo, moves and board, with the game checks: Three panes (round 2)

The legend has 6 numbered notes, and the design carries 6 badges: 1 photo, 2 moves, 3 board, 4 game checks, 5 save bar, 6 phone (12 k-num-badge in all). Frame A shows three panes in a 400/520/440 grid. Frame B has 9 state cards plus the folded tenth, "Couldn't load", and each title has a word beside its coloured dot. Frame C is one phone with a 390px viewport (414px with the bezel). The tag check found 0 unclosed or mismatched tags. None of these appear: {{holes}}, iframes, animations or transitions. In the visible text and aria-labels there are 0 em or en dashes, 0 USCF, 0 AI or model references, 0 grade or birthdate fields, 0 need questions and 0 ".5". Each of the 7 dates has its weekday: Tue, Oct 13, 2026; Sun, Sep 6 (several times); Tue, Oct 6; Wed, Sep 9, 2026; Sun, Sep 6, 2026 in the footer. The only time shown is 8:00 PM. Brand gold never appears as a text colour on a light ground: it is used only for fills, rings and underlines. Sample-data badges are on the legend, the page kicker, state 4 and state 9. The daily count reads in words: "16 of 20 scans left today · resets at midnight" on the laptop and "16 of 20 scans left today" on the phone. The decoder contract holds: 7. Qb3 is "read as Qb8 ... the only legal match, so it was fixed", the photo overlay shows the raw read text Qb8, and legality is credited to the decoder. Save, Open in lichess and Download PGN are closed with "Resolve 1 flagged move to save" in the main frame, the phone and states 2, 3 and 8, and they open only in state 1, All clear. The privacy rules hold: state 9 shows Only me selected, the other two sharing choices disabled, "Sharing a junior's game needs a guardian's OK", and no child email or grade. Overflow and clipping scan: only the intended screen-reader-only spans clip, and the 9 state cards fit their fixed height with no clipping.
